title: Taxonomy Vocabulary And Package Discovery Contract
description: Mechanism step M1 of the crate-consolidation/plugin-taxonomy-restructure master ticket (26/08/05/CRATE-CONSOLIDATION-AND-PLUGIN-TAXONOMY-RESTRUCTURE). Build ONE shared source of truth for taxonomy vocabulary (artifact/window/component directory names) and a repo-wide package discovery helper, additive-only in @semio-tech/repo-lib (framework/products/repo/modules/lib/implementations/typescript): a new 🔣️taxonomy.json data file plus a new 🟦️discovery.ts module (loadTaxonomy, areaOf, readSemioMarker, discoverPackages), exported from the package's 📦️index.ts barrel. Reconciles the two independently-hand-maintained taxonomy vocab copies (framework/os/plugin/registry script.ts's TAXONOMY_ARTIFACT_COMPONENTS vs root script.ts's POLICY_ARTIFACT_COMPONENT_DIRS) into one JSON file that both scripts will consume in a later wave. Does NOT edit either existing script — read-only reference for this ticket.
summary:
Built the shared taxonomy vocabulary + repo-wide package discovery contract for mechanism step M1, additive-only in @semio-tech/repo-lib (no existing script edited).

Files created:
- 🧰️framework/🛍️products/🦑️repo/🔨️modules/📚️lib/⚡️implementations/🟦️typescript/🔣️taxonomy.json — flat JSON vocab (roles, langs, artifactComponentDirs/artifactChildDirsExtra split, windowChildDirs, taxonomyLeafParentDirs, taxonomyLeafFilename, libWiringLineBudget, forbiddenPathSegments, packagesDirName, areas), with a `_comment` field documenting the two-list split.
- 🧰️framework/🛍️products/🦑️repo/🔨️modules/📚️lib/⚡️implementations/🟦️typescript/🟦️discovery.ts — `loadTaxonomy`, `areaOf`, `readSemioMarker`, `discoverPackages`, plus `PackageRole`/`PackageLang`/`DiscoveredPackage`/`Taxonomy` types. Resolves the JSON path via `dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))` (matching `getLibRoot` in this same package's index.ts) rather than `import.meta.dir`, since this file is included in the package's strict `tsc -p tsconfig.json` lint target (only `types: ["node"]`, no bun-types) while `📜️script.ts` files that use `import.meta.dir` are explicitly excluded from that tsconfig.

Files edited:
- 🧰️framework/🛍️products/🦑️repo/🔨️modules/📚️lib/⚡️implementations/🟦️typescript/📦️index.ts — appended `export * from "./🟦️discovery.ts";` in a new `//#region 🔣️TaxonomyDiscovery` block (no existing barrel pattern existed; this is additive only, 6 lines).
- 🧰️framework/🛍️products/🦑️repo/🔨️modules/📚️lib/⚡️implementations/🟦️typescript/🧪️index.test.ts — extended (not replaced) with 8 new tests covering loadTaxonomy/areaOf/readSemioMarker/discoverPackages, per CLAUDE.md's "extend existing test files" rule.

Vocabulary disagreement found and reconciled: framework/os/plugin/registry script.ts's `TAXONOMY_ARTIFACT_COMPONENTS` has 5 dirs (🔺diff, 🗣dsl, 🎒pack, 🔧op, 📡spr); root script.ts's `POLICY_ARTIFACT_COMPONENT_DIRS` has the same 5 plus ⚙️engine (6 total). Reconciled as `artifactComponentDirs` (the required 5, "completeness" set) + `artifactChildDirsExtra: ["⚙️engine"]` (allowed but not required), documented in the JSON's `_comment`. A second, smaller disagreement also found: registry script's inline taxonomy-leaf-parent set only unions artifact components + window children (10 dirs, missing 🎮commands/🛠tools/📌panels), while root script's explicit `POLICY_TAXONOMY_LEAF_PARENT_DIRS` constant has all 13. Used root script's fuller 13-dir list as canonical for `taxonomyLeafParentDirs`. `windowChildDirs` (5 dirs) and `taxonomyLeafFilename`/`libWiringLineBudget` (150) matched exactly between the two scripts, no reconciliation needed there. `roles`, `langs`, `forbiddenPathSegments`, and `areas` are forward-looking (this M1 step precedes the wave that extends discovery beyond plugins) and aren't literally present in either existing script today — kept as sketched, since neither script currently enumerates them.

Verification (all run synchronously):
1. `bun -e "import(...).then(m => ...)"` on the package barrel — confirmed `discoverPackages`/`loadTaxonomy`/`areaOf`/`readSemioMarker` all import as functions, no syntax/type errors at runtime.
2. `discoverPackages(repoRoot)` against the real repo — found 13 already-migrated plugins (writer, procedural, flow, cad, reasoning, sequence, animate, vcs, gis, sourcing, shooting, and others landed since the ticket was written by concurrent sessions), all with `role === "plugin"`, `area === "mixed"`. Confirms discovery walks correctly and is not hardcoded to any specific count.
3. `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` scoped to the package — 🟦️discovery.ts and 🔣️taxonomy.json (via `resolveJsonModule`) typecheck clean. Fixed two typing issues along the way: (a) `import.meta.dir` isn't declared under this tsconfig's `types: ["node"]` (no bun-types) — switched to the `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` pattern already used by 📦️index.ts; (b) `ReturnType<typeof readdirSync>` resolved to the wrong overload (`Dirent<NonSharedBuffer>` instead of `Dirent<string>`) — replaced with a `readdirSafe` helper whose return type infers directly from the specific `readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })` call. 3 pre-existing, unrelated tsc errors remain in index.ts (lines 15, 1420, 1421) — confirmed via `git diff --stat` that my changes only add lines, not touch those; out of scope for this ticket.
4. `bun nx run @semio-tech/repo-lib:test` (canonical invocation) — 100 pass / 9 fail, all 9 failures pre-existing and unrelated (dependency-boundary, ui scrollbar styling, micro-commit, playground ports/env, package boundary guards, command budgets, resolveCargoPackageName — none touch my new "loadTaxonomy"/"areaOf"/"readSemioMarker"/"discoverPackages" describe blocks, confirmed by name and by `git diff --stat` showing zero deletions). My own 8 new tests use `getWorkspaceRoot()` rather than the file's existing `process.cwd()` pattern, since nx's `test` target runs with cwd = package dir (not repo root) and several pre-existing tests appear broken by that same mismatch — out of scope to fix here, but I avoided inheriting the same bug in new tests.

Did not touch framework/os/plugin/registry's 📜️script.ts or root 📜️script.ts (read-only reference, per instructions — a later wave refactors them to consume this).
